participants.career:
I started my carrier with Premier Automobiles Ltd. and then Jyoti Ltd. for very brief periods and then joined Bharat Petroleum Corp. Ltd. (BPCL) where I worked till retirement. Ours was the first batch after nationalization. The scenario was very difficult. Earlier crude was very cheap, leading to all the consumers becoming very lax on efficiency and lagging in proper usage of petroleum products. When OPEC was formed it gave shock to all the countries by forcing crude oil prices to increase 10 to 11 times. This led to throwing India in balance of payment crises. After joining we were given training and attached to a group formed by ministry named Petroleum Consumption Action Group (later known as PCRA). our task of how to increase efficiency of petroleum product consumption at the customer end. We carried out studies at all the large and medium industry and suggested ways to conserve petroleum products. Films, leaflets, posters and films were prepared, and seminars were conducted to create awareness among consumers. 

Oil industry jobs are quite strenuous and involving. We are also frequently transferred from one place to another. I've worked in sales, customers service, safety audit, surveys at customer places for proper use and conservation of petroleum products. When I was posted at headquarters I was given all India upgradation of vehicle service stations at our petrol pumps. Which I was able to achieve at large number of locations. When I was in charge of lubricants at various locations, I was able to achieve very good sales performance against local and multinational enterprises. In my last posting I was assigned all India coordination of environmental projects. This included projects to enhance efficiency in all our activities including refinery, installations, depots and offices. We arranged third party audits of our activities. These were then becoming part of our Sustainability reports prepared every year. Then it is submitted for board approval to putting on the BPCL site for shareholders’ and public view.

participants.memory:
1. I was from Bhilai and more students were from Bhilai. We Bhilaians came every Saturday from college hostel to Bhilai. On Saturday only one time food was used to prepare at noon only. Every Saturday, there was half day in college. On one Saturday ,during the meal some students got competition that who will eat more poori. So , many students started eating. Cook was surprised to see that. At last, three students ate a big amount of poories. The student who became first , ate 50 poories, second ate 45 poories, and third was me ate 35 poories. Second day, our stomachs became upset, and we were in pain. So that was a memorial moment for all of us. 
2. We Bhilaians used to go on Monday from Bhilai to Raipur, to our college by train. The train time was at 8.45am starting from Durg station and reaching Raipur station at 9.45 am. All students generally used that train. One Monday, there was a magistrate checking. All the students climbed up the train. Nobody knew about magistrate checking. Most of the students were without ticket. So , between Kumhari station and Raipur, many students were caught by railway Authority. They were taken to the court in police van. The magistrate saw all the students and asked some questions and freed them by giving warnings not to do this in future. That day , those students could not attend the college. This was a very Memorial Day for them. Those days were students' days. Really, the student’s life was a unique life.

participants.memory:
My journey with GEC/NIT Raipur began in 1971–72 as a first-year Engineering student. I proudly cleared all my subjects in the first year, writing my answer papers in Hindi, and those early college days became some of the most memorable years of my life.

Our hostel room was often filled with 8–10 friends, and we had turned it into our own little “Music Company,” with singers and instrumentalists. We were always ready for the Hostel Day and College Gathering—music, friendship and enthusiasm were part of our everyday life.

The college gave me not only engineering education and practical learning, but also lifelong values of, teamwork, social involvement and participation in various social programs, along with friendships in the life till today.

In my fourth year, I was chosen to take up the responsibility of President of the Students’ Union. During the period when the Emergency was declared, our Principal, Shri Deshpandey, called me and seriously advised me that, officially, I should introduce myself as the President of the Students’ Welfare Committee. This was another memorable chapter of my college life and gave me valuable experience in leadership, responsibility and working with students and the college administration.

After more than five decades, I feel immense pride and gratitude to remain connected with all friends, and also as the President of the GEC–NIT Alumni Association.

GEC/NIT Raipur is not just where I studied—it is where my professional journey, leadership experience, lifelong friendships and many cherished memories began.

I may not remember all faces now but our shared moments of camaraderie, hanging out, and safety net it provided still fills me with glowing warmth and evokes sweet memories. Not having enough money to pay for movie cycle stand, cutting tea at Netaji Hotel, hopping from one friend’s place to another, doing homework together have all made them stuff of folklore. Our dedicated teachers like Dr Kamth, Professor Telang ,Professor Pillai ,Professor Ghatge, thank you for laying the foundation, shaping us what we are today.
